injuries.longComment: Paopao hasn't played since July 13 due to a right leg injury, and she remains without a timetable for a return. She can be considered week-to-week until the Dream provide an update on her progress.
injuries.shortComment: Paopao (leg) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Toronto.

injuries.longComment: Taylor will miss a third straight game due to a left groin injury. Jacy Sheldon and Gabriela Jaquez figure to retain larger roles in her absence.
injuries.shortComment: Taylor (groin) is out for Monday's game against the Storm.

injuries.longComment: Diggins has not played since early July due to a right knee injury, and her timetable for return remains unclear. She should be considered week-to-week until more information is provided as to her status going forward.
injuries.shortComment: Diggins (knee) is out for Monday's game against the Storm.

injuries.longComment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.
injuries.shortComment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: Jackson will be held out of Friday's contest after logging 11 minutes in Sunday's loss to Dallas, when she recorded one assist. Her next opportunity to play will come Thursday against the Dream.
injuries.shortComment: Jackson (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Mercury.

injuries.longComment: Beers is in the league's concussion protocol for at least one game. Nell Angloma figures to step into the backup center role behind Brittney Griner (knee), if she's available, or Olivia Nelson-Ododa.
injuries.shortComment: Beers is out for Friday's game against Phoenix with a concussion.

injuries.longComment: Kliundikova joined the Lynx for the 2025 campaign and was selected by the Tempo in the second round of the WNBA Expansion Draft ahead of the 2026 season. However, she's been playing overseas and that's where she's expected to remain for the remainder of the campaign.
injuries.shortComment: The Tempo traded Kliundikova's (not injury related) rights along with a second-round pick to the Sun in exchange for Aneesah Morrow, Myles Ehrlich of Winsidr.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Shepard turned her right ankle in the opening quarter before exiting to the locker room, and she won't return for the remainder of the contest. With the star center unavailable, Li Yueru and Awak Kuier will likely see increased playing time the rest of the way.
injuries.shortComment: Shepard (ankle) will not return to Sunday's game against the Lynx. She'll finish with one assist in five minutes.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: This will be Clark's third consecutive game on the inactive list, and her minutes will be divvied up amongst Alanna Smith and Awak Kuier. For now, Clark should be considered questionable for Wednesday's meeting with the Tempo.
injuries.shortComment: Clark (back) will remain on the sidelines for Sunday's game in Minnesota.

injuries.longComment: Verona is signed to a developmental contract, so she has only appeared in one regular-season game for Dallas during the 2026 campaign. She will now head overseas, where she will suit up for the Italian National Team for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. It's unknown whether Verona will be back with the Wings, though her departure will allow the team to sign another player to a developmental deal.
injuries.shortComment: Verona's contract was temporarily suspended by the Wings Saturday.

injuries.longComment: Stokes concludes the contest with five points (2-8 FG, 1-4 3Pt), seven rebounds and three assists in 19 minutes. Janelle Salaun figures to see extra minutes down the stretch with Stokes sidelined. The injury puts her status for Wednesday's game against the Sky in question.
injuries.shortComment: Stokes will not return to Sunday's game against the Sparks due to a neck contusion, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.

injuries.longComment: Sowah has been on the inactive list most of the season. Her next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against the Sky.
injuries.shortComment: Sowah (coach's decision) will miss Sunday's game in Los Angeles.

injuries.longComment: Prechtel has made just one appearance for the Valkyries this season, and that was back in May. Her next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Sky.
injuries.shortComment: Prechtel (coach's decision) won't play Sunday against the Sparks.

injuries.longComment: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.
injuries.shortComment: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.

injuries.longComment: The Fever should check back in with VanSlooten closer to Tuesday's tipoff to see how she's feeling. That said, she's been a healthy inactive for five consecutive contests.
injuries.shortComment: VanSlooten is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Liberty due to an illness.

injuries.longComment: Clark has been a regular on the injury report this season due to a lingering back issue. However, she hasn't missed a game since July 9 and is expected to suit up against New York. The star floor general has scored at least 19 points in six straight games, averaging 25.0 points, 9.5 assists, 4.0 rebounds and 2.0 combined steals-plus-blocks in 33.7 minutes per tilt during that time.
injuries.shortComment: Clark (back) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: Dantas struggled to stay healthy and will go ahead and address her knee issues now rather than delaying any longer. She made 12 appearances this season, posting averages of 3.3 points and 1.5 rebounds in 8.2 minutes per contest.
injuries.shortComment: Dantas underwent left knee surgery Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season, the Fever announced.

injuries.longComment: Gray will be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set for rest purposes, and her next opportunity to play will come Tuesday against the Mystics. With Jackie Young (rest) also sidelined, Jewell Loyd, Kierstan Bell, Dana Evans and Justine Pissott are all candidates to see increased playing time.
injuries.shortComment: Gray (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: After posting 23 points (6-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five rebounds and one assist over 33 minutes during the Aces' 98-87 loss to the Lynx on Saturday, Young will take a seat for the second half of Las Vegas' back-to-back set. Chelsea Gray and A'ja Wilson will also be resting, so there will be plenty of minutes available for reserves, including Dana Evans, Kierstan Bell and Brianna Turner.
injuries.shortComment: Young (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: Wilson will sit out the second half of this back-to-back set after posting 16 points, eight rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal across 33 minutes in Saturday's loss to the Lynx. Her next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Mystics. Brianna Turner and Stephanie Talbot will likely see increased playing time in Wilson's stead.
injuries.shortComment: Wilson (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Morgan has yet to suit up for Los Angeles this season. Her next chance to debut comes Tuesday against the Mercury.
injuries.shortComment: Morgan (coach's decision) is out for Sunday's game against the Valkyries.

injuries.longComment: Pili will be held out of Sunday's contest to preserve her eligibility while signed to a developmental contract. Her next opportunity to suit up will come Tuesday against the Mercury.
injuries.shortComment: Pili (coach's decision) is out for Sunday's game against the Valkyries.

injuries.longComment: With Akoa Makani unavailable, expect more minutes for Chance Gray and Jihyun Park. Akoa Makani's next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Mercury.
injuries.shortComment: Akoa Makani (ankle) won't play Sunday against the Valkyries.

injuries.longComment: Bibby, who signed with the Lynx on Aug. 1, will miss a third consecutive contest while attending to a personal matter. Her next opportunity to make her team debut will come in Portland on Wednesday.
injuries.shortComment: Bibby (personal) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wings.

injuries.longComment: out
injuries.shortComment: out

injuries.longComment: Fiebich hasn't played since July 3 due to a left foot injury, and she can be considered week-to-week until the Liberty offer another update on her rehab. In the meantime, Rebecca Allen and Marine Fauthoux will likely continue to see increased burn.
injuries.shortComment: Head coach Chris DeMarco said Sunday that Fiebich is progressing in her recovery but is still without a timetable for a return to game action, Madeline Kenney of the New York Post reports.

injuries.longComment: Plum tweaked her left calf during the second quarter of Sunday's game, and she will not rejoin her team on the court following halftime. She'll end her day with five points (2-7 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 0-1 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 14 minutes. Sami Whitcomb is poised for a larger role for the rest of Sunday's game in Plum's absence.
injuries.shortComment: Plum will not return to Sunday's game against the Mystics due to left calf tightness.

injuries.longComment: Dunn will be held out of Sunday's game in an effort to manage her eligibility while signed to a developmental deal. Her next chance to play will come Tuesday against the Sparks.
injuries.shortComment: Dunn (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Washington.

injuries.longComment: Ciezki will sit out Sunday's contest to preserve her eligibility under a developmental deal. Her next opportunity to suit up will come in Los Angeles on Tuesday.
injuries.shortComment: Ciezki (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Mystics.

injuries.longComment: Nogic had her contract temporarily suspended June 20 and will now be out for the remainder of the WNBA season, as she's slated to compete overseas in Russia with an eye on leading the Serbian national team in the EuroBasket 2027 qualifiers. The guard appeared in 16 games (seven starts) for Phoenix, averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 20.2 minutes per contest. With Nogic out of the fold for the foreseeable future, Alexa Held stands to continue benefiting from expanded opportunities in the backcourt.
injuries.shortComment: Nogic (not injury related) intends to play professionally in Russia and won't return to Phoenix this season, Aya Abdeen of TheIXSports.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Leite will end her evening with two assists and a turnover across four minutes, and for now, she should be considered questionable for Wednesday's meeting with the Lynx. Jordan Harrison started the second half in Leite's place Saturday, so Harrison stands to benefit if Leite needs to miss time.
injuries.shortComment: Leite won't return to Saturday's game against the Storm due to a left knee sprain, Sean Highkin of RoseGardenReport.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Oblak was expected to return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury Saturday, but it seems the team is taking a cautious approach with her return. That means Jordan Harrison and Holly Winterburn could see expanded roles once again. Oblak's next chance to return will come against the Lynx on Wednesday.
injuries.shortComment: Oblak (knee) is out for Saturday's game against Seattle.

injuries.longComment: Geiselsoder will represent Germany at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup, and since she's been out of the rotation for a while, she's leaving early for preparation and won't return this season. She ends the season with averages of 4.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 16.6 minutes per game in 21 appearances (nine starts).
injuries.shortComment: Geiselsoder (personal) won't return this season, according to Sean Highkin of RoseGardenReport.com.

injuries.longComment: Barker was helped to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Wings, and she's now been diagnosed with a season-ending injury. The second-year guard took on a significant role for the Fire after the club selected her in the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft. Across 26 regular-season games (15 starts), the 24-year-old averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest. Karlie Samuelson, Teja Oblak and Nyadiew Puoch are candidates for increased playing time in Barker's stead.
injuries.shortComment: The Fire announced Friday that Barker will undergo surgery to repair a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.longComment: Feagin agreed to a developmental contract with Portland on June 24 after spending time in Los Angeles. After appearing in 16 regular-season games for the Sparks in 2025, the 23-year-old played in only three regular-season contests in 2026, logging a combined 10 minutes. Feagin had yet to make her debut with the Fire, though that will now need to wait, assuming Portland keeps her on the roster moving ahead.
injuries.shortComment: Feagin (knee) was diagnosed with a torn left ACL on Thursday and will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.

injuries.longComment: After suiting up for Saturday's contest against the Fire, Mair will be sidelined for Monday's matchup with the Sky. Her next chance to suit up comes Friday against the Fire.
injuries.shortComment: Mair (coach's decision) is out for Monday's game against the Sky.

injuries.longComment: Magbegor has been dealing with a facial fracture for some time now, but she has been able to suit up for four straight games. Over those four contests, she averaged 7.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.0 steals in 19.5 minutes per game.
injuries.shortComment: Magbegor is questionable for Monday's game against the Sky due to a facial injury.

injuries.longComment: Samuelson could miss a second straight game due to a right knee injury. If she is unable to play, Zia Cooke and Jordan Horston could see expanded roles.
injuries.shortComment: Samuelson (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against the Sky.

injuries.longComment: Johnson could miss the first game of her young career due to an ankle injury. If she is unable to, Jade Melbourne and Zia Cooke could see larger roles.
injuries.shortComment: Johnson is questionable for Monday's game against the Sky due to a left ankle injury.

injuries.longComment: Sykes remains without an official timetable, so she should be viewed as week-to-week moving forward. Marina Mabrey (neck) and Isabella Harrison should continue to see increased opportunities on offense with Sykes sidelined.
injuries.shortComment: Sykes (foot) will remain on the inactive list for Monday's game in Atlanta.

injuries.longComment: Littlepage-Buggs will sit out Sunday's matchup as the Mystics manage her eligibility under a developmental pact. Her next opportunity to play will come Tuesday in Los Angeles.
injuries.shortComment: Littlepage-Buggs (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Mercury.

injuries.longComment: Laney-Hamilton was claimed off waivers by the Mystics on Saturday, two days after she was cut from the Liberty, and her next chance to make her team debut is Tuesday against the Aces. Laney-Hamilton appeared in 17 regular-season games (five starts) for New York and averaged 4.7 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.5 assists over 16.8 minutes per contest, though she was a healthy DNP for nine consecutive games from July 18 to Aug. 7.
injuries.shortComment: Laney-Hamilton (personal) is not available for Sunday's game against the Mercury.
